questions.prompt: Why does the `Transaction` model have no `INotifyPropertyChanged` and no UI logic?
options: DataGrid cannot display classes that implement `INotifyPropertyChanged`
It is pure data for the DB table; UI behavior belongs in the ViewModel
EF Core forbids entity classes from implementing any interfaces
The model is only ever used in unit tests, never in the UI
questions.explanation: The Model represents the database table and is pure data: no `INotifyPropertyChanged` and no UI logic. Notification and UI state live in the ViewModel.

questions.prompt: What is the benefit of putting the database access behind `ITransactionService`?
options: The DB logic is isolated and can be swapped for EF Core or Dapper
It lets the View call the database directly through the interface
It makes the `Transaction` class raise change notifications
It removes the need for an `ObservableCollection`
questions.explanation: The service isolates the DB logic (here simulated with an in-memory list), so it can be replaced with EF Core or Dapper later without touching the ViewModel's logic.

questions.prompt: How does `TransactionViewModel` know which row the user has selected in the DataGrid?
options: Code-behind handles `SelectionChanged` and passes the row to the ViewModel
The ViewModel reads `DataGrid.SelectedItem` through a reference to the window
The Delete button passes the row with `CommandParameter`
questions.explanation: The View binds `SelectedItem="{Binding SelectedTransaction}"`, so the selection flows into the ViewModel without any code-behind or UI reference.

questions.prompt: The ViewModel's `Delete()` calls `_service.Delete(SelectedTransaction.Id)` and then `Transactions.Remove(SelectedTransaction)`. Why the second call?
options: The service call only marks the row; `Remove` actually deletes it from the database
Without it, `CanDelete()` would throw on the next check
It is needed so `LoadCommand` can run again later
Removing it from the `ObservableCollection` updates the DataGrid
questions.explanation: The service removes the record from the data store, and removing it from the bound `ObservableCollection<Transaction>` makes the DataGrid update automatically.

questions.prompt: Put the path of a Delete action through the app in order.
steps: The user clicks the Delete button
questions.explanation: The lesson's delete flow is Button → Command → ViewModel → Service → UI updates automatically.
